# Semantic version bumper pipeline.
#
# Two jobs:
#   test — runs the full unit-test suite (node:test) so every test case
#          executes inside the CI container.
#   bump — runs the bumper end-to-end against a commit-log fixture and
#          prints the resulting version file + changelog for verification.
#
# Test cases are injected by writing an optional `test-case.env` file into
# the repo before triggering the workflow (the act harness does this); when
# absent, sensible defaults are used so the workflow also runs standalone.
name: Semantic Version Bumper

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    name: Unit tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Show node version
        run: node --version

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: node --test test/

  bump:
    name: Bump version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: test
    env:
      # Pinned date keeps the changelog output deterministic for assertions.
      RELEASE_DATE: "2026-07-01"
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure test case
        # Defaults below; a test-case.env file in the repo root overrides them.
        run: |
          VERSION_FILE=VERSION
          COMMITS_FILE=fixtures/feat-commits.txt
          if [ -f test-case.env ]; then
            echo "Loading test case overrides from test-case.env"
            # shellcheck disable=SC1091
            . ./test-case.env
          fi
          {
            echo "VERSION_FILE=$VERSION_FILE"
            echo "COMMITS_FILE=$COMMITS_FILE"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Bump version and generate changelog
        run: |
          node src/bumper.js \
            --version-file "$VERSION_FILE" \
            --commits-file "$COMMITS_FILE" \
            --changelog-file CHANGELOG.md \
            --date "$RELEASE_DATE"

      - name: Show updated files
        run: |
          echo "--- version file: $VERSION_FILE ---"
          cat "$VERSION_FILE"
          echo "--- CHANGELOG.md ---"
          cat CHANGELOG.md || echo "(no changelog generated)"

WORKFLOW = os.path.join(ROOT, ".github", "workflows", "semantic-version-bumper.yml")

def main():
    check(os.path.isfile(WORKFLOW), f"workflow file exists: {WORKFLOW}")
    with open(WORKFLOW) as f:
        wf = yaml.safe_load(f)

    # PyYAML parses the bare key `on` as boolean True.
    triggers = wf.get("on", wf.get(True))

    check("push" in triggers, "triggers include push")
    check("pull_request" in triggers, "triggers include pull_request")
    check("workflow_dispatch" in triggers, "triggers include workflow_dispatch")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end test harness: every test case runs through the GitHub Actions
# workflow via act (nektos/act), never against the script directly.
#
# For each case we:
#   1. copy the project into a fresh temp git repo,
#   2. bake in that case's fixture data (version file + test-case.env),
#   3. run `act push --rm` and append its output to act-result.txt,
#   4. assert exit code 0, exact expected version output, and that every
#      job reports "Job succeeded".
set -u

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
RESULT_FILE="$ROOT/act-result.txt"
: > "$RESULT_FILE"

PASS=0
FAIL=0

fail() {
  echo "  ASSERTION FAILED: $1"
  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
  return 1
}

# make_repo <dest> — copy project files into a fresh git repo at <dest>
make_repo() {
  local dest="$1"
  mkdir -p "$dest"
  cp -r "$ROOT/src" "$ROOT/test" "$ROOT/fixtures" "$ROOT/.github" "$dest/"
  cp "$ROOT/.actrc" "$ROOT/VERSION" "$dest/"
  git -C "$dest" init -q -b master
  git -C "$dest" -c user.email=ci@example.com -c user.name=ci add -A
  git -C "$dest" -c user.email=ci@example.com -c user.name=ci commit -qm "test fixture repo"
}

# run_case <name> <setup-fn> <expected-version> <expected-bump-line>
run_case() {
  local name="$1" setup="$2" expected_version="$3" expected_line="$4"
  local dir output rc case_ok=1
  dir="$(mktemp -d /tmp/bumper-act-XXXXXX)"
  echo "=== Test case: $name ==="

  make_repo "$dir"
  "$setup" "$dir"
  # commit the case-specific fixture data too
  git -C "$dir" -c user.email=ci@example.com -c user.name=ci add -A
  git -C "$dir" -c user.email=ci@example.com -c user.name=ci commit -qm "case: $name" --allow-empty

  output="$(cd "$dir" && act push --rm 2>&1)"
  rc=$?

  {
    echo "================================================================"
    echo "=== TEST CASE: $name"
    echo "=== expected NEW_VERSION=$expected_version | act exit code: $rc"
    echo "================================================================"
    echo "$output"
    echo
  } >> "$RESULT_FILE"

  # 1. act must exit 0
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { fail "act exited with code $rc (expected 0)"; case_ok=0; }

  # 2. exact machine-readable version line
  echo "$output" | grep -qF "NEW_VERSION=$expected_version" \
    || { fail "output missing exact 'NEW_VERSION=$expected_version'"; case_ok=0; }

Zero-dependency Node.js tool that reads a semantic version from a plain
`VERSION` file or a `package.json`, classifies conventional commit messages

back, prepends a grouped `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and prints the new version as
